creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 14, item 1.

Passing `--mock-response` twice mocks only the last pattern; requests matching the earlier one go to the real service with no warning. A test run of a CLI that makes two POSTs sent the first to the live API with a dummy key and got a 401. Nothing says the flag is single-valued: `-h` describes it in the singular, and guide/global-flags says rad "checks for defined mock responses".

```
$ rad mock.rad --mock-response '.*/a:a.json' --mock-response '.*/b:b.json'
Querying url: http://127.0.0.1:9/a          # went live
Mocking response for url (matched ".*/b"): http://127.0.0.1:9/b
```

The value is also split with `strings.Split(v, ":")` keeping parts 0 and 1, so a pattern containing a colon breaks silently: `--mock-response 'http://127.0.0.1:9/a:a.json'` becomes pattern `http`, which matches every URL, and file `//127.0.0.1`. A value with no colon panics (index out of range), which is main-board RAD-114 (`3d86PibU`); the same fix closes it.

All three reproduce on main. Both regressions date from 043d1047 ("Replace pflag with Ra"): before it the flag was a `MockResponseSlice` that collected every occurrence and split on the last colon. That type is still in `core/args_mock.go`, unused. Make the flag repeatable again, split on the last colon, reject a value with no colon, and match patterns in flag order so it is defined which mock wins when two match (the requester's map leaves that undefined).

Where: `core/flags_global.go:238` (single string arg), `core/runner.go:350-356` (split), `core/requester.go:146` (pattern map).
title: --mock-response keeps only its last occurrence and splits on the first colon
